name: ESP32 ULP Coprocessor
description: The `esp32_ulp` component builds a program for the ESP32's low power coprocessor, embeds it in the firmware and runs it. The coprocessor keeps running while the main CPU is in deep sleep, so it can poll pins, sample the ADC or talk to a sensor at very low power and wake the main CPU when something needs attention.

config_entries.label: Sources
config_entries.description: The C (`.c`) and assembly (`.S`) files that make up the program, relative to the YAML file. Header files (`.h`) may be listed too; they are copied next to the sources so the program can include them. File names must be unique.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation. Needed for the lambda calls below.

config_entries.label: Reserve Memory
config_entries.description: Bytes of RTC slow memory (LP memory) reserved for the program, its variables and its stack. Defaults to `4096`. The maximum is `8176` on the S2/S3, `16352` on the C5/C6 and `31088` on the P4. On the S2/S3 the value must be a multiple of 16, as the stack starts at its end.

config_entries.label: Run On Boot
config_entries.description: Load and start the program during setup. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, call `load_and_run()` from a lambda. However it was started, a running program is left alone after a deep-sleep wake and its variables keep their values.

config_entries.label: Wakeup From Sleep
config_entries.description: Allow the program to wake the main CPU from deep sleep. Defaults to `true`.

config_entries.label: Wakeup Period
config_entries.description: ***Optional* on the LP core when `wakeup_sources` is set**: How often the timer starts the program, from `1us` to about 71 minutes. The program runs to completion each time; returning from `main` halts the coprocessor until the next period.

config_entries.label: Wakeup Sources
config_entries.description: LP core only (ESP32-C5/C6/P4). Additional events that start the program: `hp_cpu` (started once by the main CPU), `lp_io` (LP IO interrupt), `lp_uart` (LP UART activity) or `etm` (ETM event). The LP timer is used automatically when `wakeup_period` is set.
